prompt: The polynomial $p(x) = (x - 5)(x + 2)$ crosses the $x$-axis twice. What is the LARGER of the two zeros?
hint: A product is zero when one of its factors is zero.

hints.text: A product is zero when one of its factors is zero.
Set each factor to zero: $x - 5 = 0$ gives $x = 5$, and $x + 2 = 0$ gives $x = -2$.
The zeros are $5$ and $-2$, so the larger is $5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read the sign backwards
steps: A factor $(x - 5)$ hides the zero $+5$ — the sign flips.
On a number line those sit at $-2$ and $5$, and 5 is farther right.
